name: Irad
overview: Irad is a male biblical figure identified as the son of Enoch, as recorded in Genesis 4:18. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His mention is brief, focusing primarily on his lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Irad is a proper name meaning "fugitive." It was not given by God but appears in the Scripture to identify this individual specifically in Genesis 4:18.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Irad is the son of Enoch and the father of Mehujael, establishing a generational link within the early descendants mentioned in Genesis 4:18. These relationships are explicitly stated in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Irad's significance lies in his place within the genealogical record of early humanity following the fall, as documented in Genesis. His mention helps trace the lineage from Cain through successive generations, providing a framework for understanding the development of early families in the biblical narrative. Though details about his life are sparse, his role as a link in this genealogy underlines the importance of family lines in God's providential history.
